# Can a single contact point be set as the system root to enforce zero velocity and acceleration for multiple contacts using RNEA?

> **Current answer:** Project members indicated that placing the system root at a single contact point can be addressed using RNEA, but since a system has only one root, this method cannot handle multiple contacts simultaneously. This approach is very restrictive. Multiple acceleration-based holonomic constraints should be applied through TSID or general QP optimization. The thread mentions Schur-complement paths and using inertial matrix and contact Jacobian structures. The original thread did not implement or retest these solutions, so it is an architecture boundary and not directly replicable for multi-contact controllers.

## Key terms

- Complete constraint (holonomic constraint) (完整约束)
- Multi-contact (多接触)
- Schur complement (舒尔补)
- Task-space inverse dynamics (TSID) (任务空间逆动力学)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to construct a model.njoints-length and joint-local-frame expression for rnea fext when there is no joint in the contact frame?
- Does directly using CRBA, nonLinearEffects, and frame Jacobian manually write forces and torques equivalent and efficient compared to RNEA?
- Can multiple fixed contact points' zero velocity/acceleration constraints be addressed by setting one contact point as RNEA root?
- RNEA requires a local-frame fext for each joint, but physical contact occurs in a foot-tip frame without a joint.
- Directly calling SE3 act on aligned_vector<Force> causes a compilation error, as the vector lacks se3Action.

## Environment

- 2022 Pinocchio C++; floating-base quadruped; foot-tip contact frames; author ultimately used CentroidalModelRbdConversions.cpp from OCS2 commit 3566993.

## Priority diagnostics

- First find the parent joint and relative placement of the contact frame; then transform the wrench to the joint local frame.
- Distinguish between a single force element and a force vector of length model.njoints.
- Compare the manually written floating-base equations with RNEA output, and separately evaluate whether kinematic-tree sparsity was utilized.

## Possible causes

- Directly placing contact-frame force into RNEA without transforming the action point or local expression.
- Incorrectly calling SE3 action on an entire std::vector<Force>.
- Manually writing dense CRBA/Jacobian operations without leveraging RNEA's kinematic-tree recursive sparsity.

## Attempts

- Maintainer suggests using kMt.act(f_t); the author then uses the parent-joint force/wrench construction from OCS2 fixed submission.
- Another participant manually wrote floating-base equations using CRBA, nonLinearEffects, and frame Jacobians; the original author compared results with RNEA.
- Participants discussed the solution boundaries for single-contact re-rooting and multi-contact acceleration-level holonomic constraints.

## Effective fixes

- Establish fext elements based on the contact frame's parent joint; transform the world-frame force to the joint frame, and construct moment via joint-to-contact translation × force; add joint-frame contact torque for 6D contact.
- Apply the transformation to a single pinocchio::Force, not to aligned_vector<Force>.

- Original author confirmed the solution after citing the referenced OCS2 code.
- Original author reported that the manually written floating-base equations and RNEA results are very close, but no error or speed benchmark was provided.
- Multi-contact QP/TSID design discussion is not provided in this thread for replication.
